120: Search endpoint. This tool takes a search term for a symbol or company name, then looks up matching instruments. It is typically used to find the correct ticker before requesting data, and it returns the matches with their symbols, names, types, and regions.
121: Fetch a time series daily. This tool takes a ticker symbol, then retrieves its daily price history. It is typically used for charting or analysis over days, and it returns each trading day's open, high, low, close, and volume for the requested symbol.
122: Fetch a time series daily adjusted. This tool takes a ticker symbol, then retrieves its daily price history with values adjusted for splits and dividends. It is typically used for accurate historical analysis, and it returns each day's adjusted open, high, low, close, and volume.
123: Fetch a time series intraday. This tool takes a ticker symbol and an interval, then retrieves intraday price history at that granularity. It is typically used for short-term analysis, and it returns each interval's open, high, low, close, and volume within the trading day.
124: Fetch a time series monthly. This tool takes a ticker symbol, then retrieves its monthly price history. It is typically used for long-horizon analysis, and it returns each month's open, high, low, close, and volume for the requested symbol.
125: Fetch a time series monthly adjusted. This tool takes a ticker symbol, then retrieves its monthly price history adjusted for splits and dividends. It is typically used for long-term return analysis, and it returns each month's adjusted open, high, low, close, and volume.
126: Fetch a time series weekly. This tool takes a ticker symbol, then retrieves its weekly price history. It is typically used for medium-horizon analysis, and it returns each week's open, high, low, close, and volume for the requested symbol.
127: Fetch a time series weekly adjusted. This tool takes a ticker symbol, then retrieves its weekly price history adjusted for splits and dividends. It is typically used for medium-term return analysis, and it returns each week's adjusted open, high, low, close, and volume.
128: Fetch top gainers and losers. This tool takes no specific input and retrieves the stocks with the largest gains and declines for the session. It is typically used to spot notable movers, and it returns the leading gainers and losers with their prices and percentage changes.
129: Adds file contents to the staging area. This tool takes one or more file paths in the repository, then stages their current contents so they will be included in the next commit. It is typically used before committing, and it returns confirmation of the paths that were added to the staging area.
130: Switches branches. This tool takes the name of an existing branch, then checks it out so the working tree reflects that branch. It is typically used to move between lines of development, and it returns confirmation of the branch that is now active after the switch.
131: Records changes to the repository. This tool takes a commit message and commits the currently staged changes, creating a new commit in the repository history. It is typically used to save a unit of work, and it returns the identifier and summary of the commit that was created.
132: Creates a new branch from an optional base branch. This tool takes a name for the new branch and optionally a base to start from, then creates that branch in the repository. It is typically used to begin a new line of work, and it returns confirmation of the branch that was created.
133: Shows differences between branches or commits. This tool takes two references such as branches or commit identifiers, then computes the changes between them. It is typically used to review what differs, and it returns the diff describing the added and removed lines across the affected files.
134: Shows changes that are staged for commit. This tool takes no input and reports the differences currently staged in the index relative to the last commit. It is typically used to review what will be committed next, and it returns the staged diff across the affected files.
135: Shows changes in the working directory that are not yet staged. This tool takes no input and reports the modifications present in the working tree that have not been added to the staging area. It is typically used before staging, and it returns the unstaged diff across the affected files.
136: Shows the commit logs. This tool takes optional paging or range options, then retrieves the repository's commit history. It is typically used to review past work, and it returns the commits in order with their identifiers, authors, dates, and messages.
137: Unstages all staged changes. This tool takes no input and removes every change currently in the staging area, returning those modifications to an unstaged state without discarding the edits themselves. It is typically used to redo staging, and it returns confirmation once the index has been reset.
138: Shows the contents of a commit. This tool takes a commit identifier, then retrieves that commit's details. It is typically used to inspect a specific change, and it returns the commit's metadata together with the diff of what it changed across the affected files.
139: Shows the working tree status. This tool takes no input and reports the current state of the repository. It is typically used to see what has changed, and it returns which files are staged, modified but unstaged, or untracked, along with the current branch.
140: Search for files in Google Drive. This tool takes a search query with optional filters, then looks for matching files in the user's Drive. It is typically used to locate a document, and it returns each match with its name, identifier, type, and other basic file details.
141: Get directions between two points. This tool takes an origin and a destination with an optional travel mode, then computes a route between them. It is typically used for navigation, and it returns the route with its distance, estimated duration, and step-by-step directions.
142: Calculate travel distance and time for multiple origins and destinations. This tool takes lists of origins and destinations with a travel mode, then computes a matrix of results. It is typically used for planning across many pairs, and it returns the distance and estimated time for each origin-destination pair.
143: Get elevation data for locations on the earth. This tool takes one or more latitude-longitude coordinates, then looks up the terrain elevation at each. It is typically used for mapping or route analysis, and it returns the elevation value for every requested location.
144: Convert an address into geographic coordinates. This tool takes a textual address, then geocodes it into map coordinates. It is typically used before plotting or routing, and it returns the resulting latitude and longitude along with the matched, formatted address.
145: Get detailed information about a specific place. This tool takes a place identifier, then retrieves that location's full record. It is typically used after a search, and it returns details such as the name, address, coordinates, category, opening hours, and contact information where available.
146: Convert coordinates into an address. This tool takes a latitude-longitude pair, then reverse-geocodes it into a human-readable location. It is typically used to label a point on a map, and it returns the formatted address and its components for the supplied coordinates.
147: Search for places using Google Places API. This tool takes a place query with optional location context, then searches for matching places. It is typically used to find businesses or landmarks, and it returns each result with its name, address, coordinates, and basic place details.
148: Retrieves logs for a specific Actor run. Returns the log content as plain text. This tool takes the identifier of an Actor run, then fetches the log output recorded during that run, returning the collected log as plain text so the run's progress and any messages can be reviewed.
149: Get upcoming LoL match schedules. This tool takes optional filters such as league or date range, then retrieves scheduled upcoming League of Legends matches. It is typically used to follow esports fixtures, and it returns each match with its teams, league, and scheduled start time.
